title: Expansion Microscopy: Protocols for Imaging Proteins and RNA in Cells and Tissues
markdown:
## Protocol: A 2018 Current Protocols in Cell Biology workflow covering protein-retention expansion microscopy and expansion FISH, with AcX and LabelX anchoring, approximately 4.5-fold hydrogel expansion, and confocal or light-sheet imaging of cells and tissues

### Overview

This protocol outlines a workflow for protein-retention expansion microscopy (proExM) and expansion fluorescence in situ hybridization (ExFISH). It utilizes AcX and LabelX anchoring chemistries to achieve approximately 4.5-fold linear hydrogel expansion. The procedure covers sample preparation for both cultured cells and tissues, including fixation, optional immunostaining, gelation, digestion, and final expansion. Imaging can be performed using confocal or light-sheet microscopy.

### Materials/Reagents

1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH), 30% (v/v) ethanol, 10 mg/ml sterile fibronectin in PBS, 4% (w/v) paraformaldehyde (PFA), optional glutaraldehyde, 100 mM glycine, 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100, blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum in 0.1% Triton X-100/PBS), Acryloyl-X SE (AcX)/DMSO stock, gelling solution components (Stock X, APS, TEMED, water, 4-hydroxy-TEMPO/4HT for tissues), digestion buffer (Proteinase K at 8 U/ml), 10% neutral buffered formalin, 70% (v/v) ethanol, 20 mM MOPS buffer, LabelX, VA-044 initiator, alkaline buffer for post-expansion staining.

### Equipment

12-mm round coverslips, removable-chamber cover glasses (e.g., Grace Bio Labs Culturewell, Thermo Fisher Lab-Tek), 35-mm petri dishes, glass slides, spacers (stacks of coverslips), Paraﬁlm, razor blades, forceps, fine-tipped pipettes, soft paintbrushes, vacuum desiccator, nitrogen gas line, incubators (37°C, 60°C, 4°C), vibratome or cryostat/cryotome, dissection microscope, wide-field microscope, confocal or light-sheet microscope.

### Safety & Sterility

Paraformaldehyde is a potential carcinogen; handle in a chemical hood. Maintain sterile conditions during cell culture substrate preparation and plating. Store samples in the dark when specified to preserve fluorescence. Use appropriate personal protective equipment when handling chemicals such as KOH, PFA, and DMSO.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare 1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) in water and 30% (v/v) ethanol in water. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare 10 mg/ml sterile fibronectin in Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare 4% (w/v) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS; for stronger fixation, prepare a mixture of 4% (w/v) PFA and 0.1% (w/v) glutaraldehyde in PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare 100 mM glycine in PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100 in PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare blocking buffer by mixing 5% (v/v) normal donkey serum in 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100 in PBS. Store up to 1 month or longer at 4°C. Ensure the serum source matches the animal host of the secondary antibodies; use other sera if secondary antibodies are from different animals. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare Acryloyl-X SE (AcX)/DMSO stock solution according to the provided recipe. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare the gelling solution for proExM of cultured cells according to the provided recipe. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Prepare the digestion buffer according to the provided recipe. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->

## Cell Culture Substrate Preparation

### Substrate Prep

1. Treat 12-mm round coverslips with 1 M KOH in water for 30 min, rinse with water three times, and store in 30% (v/v) ethanol in water. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Air-dry the cleaned 12-mm round coverslips in a sterile environment (e.g., biosafety cabinet), place them in a 35-mm petri dish, and treat with 10 mg/ml sterile fibronectin in PBS for 30 min at 37°C. Remove the fibronectin solution immediately before cell plating. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->

## Cell Culture

### Culture

1. Plate and culture cells on the surface of either the 12-mm coverslips or removable-chamber cover glass to a confluency of 50% to 80% in a humidified incubator set at 5% CO2 and 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->

## Cell Fixation

### Fixation

1. Replace the cell culture medium with 4% (w/v) PFA in PBS and incubate for 10 min at room temperature. CAUTION: Perform this step in a chemical hood as PFA is a potential carcinogen. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Remove the PFA solution and wash the cells for 5 min with 100 mM glycine in PBS to quench the fixation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Remove the glycine solution and wash the cells twice for 5 min each with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If necessary, store fixed cells in the dark at 4°C in PBS for up to several weeks before proceeding to the next steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->

## Immunostaining (Optional)

### Immunostaining

1. Permeabilize the fixed cells by applying 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100 in PBS at room temperature for 15 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Apply blocking buffer at room temperature for 15 min to reduce nonspecific antibody binding. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
3. Incubate the cells with primary antibodies in the blocking buffer at the appropriate concentration. Incubate on a shaker at low speed for 1 hr to overnight, at room temperature or 4°C, depending on antibody specifications. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
4. Remove the antibody solution and wash four times, each time for 5 min, with blocking buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
5. Incubate the cells with secondary antibodies in blocking buffer on a shaker at low speed for 2 to 4 hr at room temperature or overnight at 4°C. If using dye-conjugated antibodies, refer to Support Protocol 2 for dye compatibility with pre-expansion staining proExM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->
6. Remove the antibody solution and wash four times, each time for 5 min, with blocking buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If necessary, store the samples in the dark at 4°C in PBS for up to several weeks before proceeding to the next steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S07 -->

## Gelation (Cultured Cells)

### AcX Treatment

1. Replace the sample buffer (e.g., blocking buffer if immunostained) with 0.1 mg/ml Acryloyl-X SE (AcX) in PBS. Prepare this AcX solution by diluting the 10 mg/ml AcX/DMSO stock solution 1:100 in PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. Leave the cells in the 0.1 mg/ml AcX solution for 2 to 3 hr at room temperature without shaking. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->

### Chamber Construction

1. Construct the gelation chamber by placing two spacers on a slide, separated by a distance large enough to fit the sample cover glass between them. Use thin, flat objects like stacks of coverslips as spacers (e.g., two No. 1.5 coverslips have a height of ~0.30–0.38 mm). Adjust spacer height to match the cell culture substrate height, ensuring the total gel thickness [spacer height - substrate height] is at least 0.15 mm. Adhere spacers to the slide with a droplet of water. If using a removable-chamber cover glass, the cover glass and gasket serve as the chamber and spacer; remove the upper structure using a removal tool (Sigma, cat. no. GBL 103259). For the lid, use a thick, robust coverslip (e.g., No. 2) wrapped in Paraﬁlm to prevent sticking; ensure the Paraﬁlm surface is flat, clean, and fold-free. Finish preparing the chamber and lid before the next step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S01 -->

### Gelling Solution Prep

1. After incubating cells in AcX solution, wash the cells twice, each time for 15 min, with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S01 -->
2. Begin thawing the components for the gelling solution for proExM (Stock X, APS, and TEMED stock solutions). Keep these solutions chilled in an ice bath or on a cold block at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S02 -->
3. Create the gelling solution for proExM by mixing Stock X, water, TEMED stock solution, and APS stock solution in a 47:1:1:1 ratio in a microcentrifuge tube, adding APS last, and vortexing for a few seconds. Scale the amount to fill the gelation chamber (e.g., 200 µl for a 22 × 22 × 0.38 mm void). Keep the mixed solution chilled at 4°C, avoiding excessive warming by holding the lid rather than the body of the tube. Complete subsequent steps within 5 min to prevent premature gelation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S03 -->

### Gelation

1. Immediately after the previous step, remove the PBS from the cells using a pipet
and add a small amount of the mixed gelling solution to the cells on the cell culture
substrate. If a removable-chamber cover glass is used, remove the PBS and add the
gelling solution to ﬁll in the chamber, then continue to step 22. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T3-S01 -->
2. Use forceps to place the cell culture substrate (with cells facing upward) between the spacers in the gelation chamber. Slightly press the substrate down to hold it in place. If gelling solution flows away, reapply a small amount. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T3-S02 -->
3. Add a 20 µl droplet of gelling solution to one side of the Paraﬁlm-covered lid, flip it over so the droplet hangs due to surface tension, and slowly lower the lid to fuse with the gelling solution on the sample. Continue lowering until the lid rests on the spacers. Ensure no air pockets are introduced. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T3-S03 -->
4. Using a pipet with a fine tip, add additional gelling solution to both open sides of the chamber until the space between the lid, spacers, and slide is filled. Capillary forces should evenly fill the void. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T3-S04 -->
5. Place the gelation chamber in an incubator at 37°C for 1 hr for polymerization. Do not tilt or shake the chamber during transfer or gelation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T3-S05 -->

## Digestion (Cultured Cells)

### Post-Gelation

1. Take the gelation chamber out of the incubator. Slowly insert a razor blade between the lid and spacers to pry the lid off. Once separated, use the razor blade to remove the spacers. If using a removable-chamber cover glass, remove the lid and peel off the black gasket without removing the gel from the cover glass. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S01 -->
2. Using a razor blade, trim the gel to a small volume around the sample to keep it compact and aid in finding cells. Remove the cell culture substrate and gel together from the glass slide. If using a removable-chamber cover glass, trim the gel but do not remove it from the cover glass. Trim the gel into an asymmetric shape to easily gauge orientation in later steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare digestion buffer as described in Reagents and Solutions, with a final Proteinase K (ProK) concentration of 8 U/ml. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S03 -->
4. Since the gel will expand by about 1.5× during digestion, choose a suitably large container (e.g., petri dish). Use a separate container for each sample to avoid mix-ups. Place the cell culture substrate with the gel in the digestion buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S04 -->

## Tissue Preparation & Immunostaining

### Tissue Slicing

1. After fixation, if tissues are thicker than 200 µm, cut them into <200 µm slices using a vibratome. Alternatively, for cryostat slicing, cryoprotect tissue by immersing it in sinking solution until it sinks, freeze using dry ice and 2-methylbutane, embed in OCT, M-1, or another matrix, and slice using a cryotome. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If necessary, store fixed tissues or tissue slices in the dark at 4°C in PBS for up to several weeks before proceeding. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S02 -->

### Immunostaining

1. Permeabilize the fixed tissue by applying 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100 in PBS at room temperature for 15 min, then apply blocking buffer at room temperature for 6 hr. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S01 -->
2. Incubate the tissues with primary antibodies in the blocking buffer. Incubate on a shaker at low speed overnight at room temperature or 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S02 -->
3. Remove the antibody solution and wash four times, each time for 30 min, with blocking buffer to remove unbound primary antibodies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S03 -->
4. Incubate the tissues with secondary antibodies in the blocking buffer on a shaker at low speed overnight at room temperature or 4°C. If using dye-conjugated antibodies, refer to Support Protocol 2 for dye performance and compatibility with pre-expansion staining proExM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S04 -->
5. Remove the antibody solution and wash four times, each time for 30 min, with blocking buffer to remove unbound secondary antibodies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Move to the gelation steps immediately after washing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If necessary, store the samples in the dark at 4°C in PBS for up to several weeks before gelation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S07 -->

## Gelation (Intact Tissues)

### AcX Treatment

1. Prepare Acryloyl-X SE (AcX)/DMSO stock solution, monomer solution (Stock X), TEMED stock solution, ammonium persulfate (APS) stock, and 4-hydroxy-TEMPO (4HT) solution as instructed in Reagents and Solutions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S01 -->
2. Replace the sample buffer (e.g., blocking buffer if immunostained) with 0.1 mg/ml Acryloyl-X SE (AcX) in PBS. Prepare this by diluting the 10 mg/ml AcX/DMSO stock solution 1:100 in PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S02 -->
3. Leave the tissues in the AcX solution for >6 hr (overnight is acceptable) at room temperature without shaking. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S03 -->

### Chamber Construction

1. Construct the gelation chamber by placing two spacers on a slide, separated from each other. Use thin, flat objects like stacks of coverslips as spacers (e.g., two No. 1.5 coverslips have a height of ~0.30–0.38 mm). Adjust spacer height to accommodate tissue thickness, ensuring the total gel thickness (spacer height) is at least 0.15 mm. Adhere spacers to the slide with a droplet of water. For the lid, use a thick, robust coverslip (e.g., No. 2) wrapped in Paraﬁlm to prevent sticking; ensure the surface is flat, clean, and fold-free. Finish preparing the chamber and lid before the next step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T1-S01 -->

### Gelling Solution Prep

1. After incubating tissues in AcX solution, wash the tissues twice, each time for 15 min, with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T2-S01 -->
2. Begin thawing the components for the gelling solution for proExM: Stock X, 4HT, APS, and TEMED stock solutions. Keep these solutions chilled in an ice bath or on a cold block at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T2-S02 -->
3. Add Stock X, 4HT, TEMED, and APS in a 47:1:1:1 ratio in this order (APS last) into a microcentrifuge tube, and vortex for a few seconds. Scale the amount to the size of the gelation chamber and tissue, ensuring at least a 100-fold excess in volume (e.g., at least 400 µl for a 100-μm mouse brain coronal slice). Add APS last to prevent premature polymerization. Keep the mixed solution chilled at 4°C, avoiding excessive warming by holding the lid. Complete subsequent steps within 5 min to prevent premature gelation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T2-S03 -->

### Gelation

1. Immediately after mixing, use a soft paintbrush to transfer and immerse the tissues in the gelling solution in the microcentrifuge tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S01 -->
2. Keep the microcentrifuge tube containing the sample and gelling solution at 4°C in the dark for 30 min. After this incubation, complete subsequent steps within 5 min to prevent premature gelation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S02 -->
3. Use a paintbrush to transfer and place the tissue slice between the spacers in the gelation chamber. Ensure the slice lies flat without wrinkles. First add a 20 µl droplet of gelling solution between the spacers, transfer the slice into the droplet, and use the paintbrush to slowly flatten the tissue onto the glass surface. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S03 -->
4. Add a 20 µl droplet of gelling solution to one side of the lid, flip it over so the droplet hangs due to surface tension, and slowly lower the lid to fuse with the gelling solution on the sample. Continue lowering until the lid rests on the spacers. Ensure no air pockets are introduced. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S04 -->
5. Using a pipettor and fine pipet tip, add additional gelling solution to both open sides of the chamber until the space between the lid, spacers, and slide is filled. Capillary forces will evenly fill the chamber. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S05 -->
6. Place the gelation chamber in an incubator at 37°C for 2 hr for polymerization. Do not tilt or shake the chamber during transfer or gelation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S06 -->

## Digestion (Intact Tissues)

### Post-Gelation

1. Take the gelation chamber out of the incubator. Slowly insert a razor blade between the lid and spacers to pry the lid open. Once separated, use the razor blade to remove the spacers in a similar fashion. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S01 -->
2. Using a razor blade, trim off any excess gel. Trimming keeps the gel compact and aids in finding regions of interest. Trim the gel into an asymmetric shape to easily gauge orientation in later steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare digestion buffer as described in Reagents and Solutions, with a final Proteinase K (ProK) concentration of 8 U/ml. Prepare enough buffer to have at least a 10-fold excess in volume compared to the gel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S03 -->
4. Use a paintbrush to wet the gel and its sides with digestion buffer. Wait 10 to 30 sec until the buffer soaks the gel border. This aids in accessing the gel bottom with the paintbrush to peel it from the glass substrate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S04 -->
5. Peel off the gel by gently probing the space between the gel and the glass surface with a fine paintbrush. Since the gel will expand to about 1.5× during digestion, choose a suitably large container (e.g., petri dish or 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube for small samples). Use separate containers filled with digestion buffer for each sample. Leave gels immersed in digestion buffer for >8 hr (overnight is acceptable) at room temperature in the dark. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S05 -->

## Storage and Expansion

### Storage

1. Remove the digestion buffer and add PBS. Store the gel at 4°C in the dark if storage for later imaging is desired. Be cautious not to suck up the gel while pipetting. The embedded tissue is slightly scattering at this stage; changing the incident angle of light might help locate it. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B11-T0-S01 -->
2. If transferring the gel to another container (e.g., for trimming or imaging), use a paintbrush of suitable size to pick up and move the gel. Add some PBS to the new container to avoid sample dehydration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B11-T0-S02 -->

### Trimming

1. Before expanding, trim the gel to the minimum size necessary. Use a dissection microscope or low-magnification wide-field microscope to locate the region of interest. Temporarily remove most surrounding liquid to minimize movement. Under the microscope, use a razor blade to cut and remove gel outside the region of interest. Trim the gel into an asymmetric shape to deduce orientation. Ensure the gel is trimmed to a reasonable size for handling, as expansion will increase linear size by 2× to 2.5× (total ~4.5×). Transfer the gel with the region of interest to a container large enough to contain the expanded gel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B11-T1-S01 -->

### Expansion

1. Fill the container, immerse the gel in water, and wait for 20 min. Replace with fresh water and wait another 20 min. Repeat once more (three 20-min exchanges total). The sample should be fully expanded and optically cleared. For long-term imaging, perform sample mounting after expansion and before imaging to prevent drifting and maintain working distance. For quick checks (<5 min), mounting is typically unnecessary; on an inverted microscope, temporarily remove water around the gel with a pipet to prevent sliding. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B11-T2-S01 -->
2. If transferring the expanded gel to a new container, handle with care as it is delicate. Remove most surrounding water, then use a brush to move the gel onto a clean glass coverslip in the same container. Gently lift the coverslip with forceps. Transfer the gel by slowly brushing it off the coverslip to the new container. This method can also flip the gel if it is facing the wrong direction. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B11-T2-S02 -->

## Thick Tissue Protocol Modifications

### Thick Tissue Processing

1. Generate tissue samples as outlined in steps 1 to 7 of Basic Protocol 2, which can be used for thicker tissue samples. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B12-T0-S01 -->
2. For the AcX step, use a slightly acidic buffer (e.g., MES-buffered saline, MBS) to suppress NHS ester reactivity for deeper penetration. Dilute the 10 mg/ml AcX/DMSO stock solution 1:100 in MBS. Leave tissue in AcX/MBS solution for up to 24 hr at room temperature, depending on thickness (e.g., 24 hr for a 500-μm brain slice). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B12-T0-S02 -->
3. For gelling solution preparation, increase the amount of 4HT by 50% (i.e., 47:1.5 ratio between Stock X and 4HT) for longer inhibition of polymerization. For incubation, submerge the sample in gelling solution for 45 to 60 min (instead of 30 min) at 4°C before transferring to the gelation chamber. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B12-T0-S03 -->
4. For digestion, perform a longer and/or stronger digestion. ProK digestion can be carried out for a longer time and/or at higher temperatures (up to 50° to 60°C), depending on tissue composition and cross-linking. For a 250-μm thick mouse brain slice, digest in digestion buffer at room temperature for 1 day, exchange with fresh buffer, and digest for another day. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B12-T0-S04 -->

## Post-Expansion Immunostaining

### Post-Expansion Staining

1. Soak the sample in alkaline buffer for 15 min, then replace with fresh alkaline buffer of the same composition. Place the sample in an autoclavable container (e.g., polypropylene bottle) with the lid slightly open for pressure relief. Autoclave on liquid sterilization mode at 121°C for 1 hr. The sample will expand visibly during this and subsequent steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S01 -->
2. Let the sample cool to room temperature and wash twice, each time for 15 min, with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S02 -->
3. Incubate the sample with primary antibodies in 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100 plus 5% (v/v) normal donkey serum in PBS (blocking buffer) on a shaker at low speed overnight at room temperature or 4°C. Ensure the serum source matches the animal host of the secondary antibodies; use other sera if secondary antibodies are from different animals. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S03 -->
4. Remove the primary antibody solution and wash four times, each time for 30 min, with blocking buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S04 -->
5. Incubate the sample with fluorescently labeled secondary antibody of choice in the blocking buffer on a shaker at low speed overnight at room temperature or 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S05 -->
6. Remove the secondary antibody solution and wash four times, each time for 30 min, with blocking buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S06 -->
7. Replace the buffer with PBS for storage (up to several weeks) if desired. Expand to the final factor of 4.5× with three 20-min washes in water, then proceed with imaging. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B13-T0-S07 -->

## ExFISH Cell Culture & LabelX

### Cell Culture

1. Grow cells as desired. For ease of gelation, imaging, and handling, use 16-well Culturewell removable-chamber cover glasses (Grace Bio Labs, Sigma cat. no. GBL112358) for ExFISH. For single-molecule FISH (smFISH) before gelation, plate cells in 8-well Nunc Lab-Tek chambered cover glasses (Thermo Fisher, cat. no. 155411). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T0-S01 -->

### Fixation & Permeabilization

1. Wash cells once with PBS warmed to 37°C to avoid heat shock. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T1-S01 -->
2. Add 10% neutral buffered formalin and fix cells for 10 min at room temperature. Wash with PBS twice, each time for 2 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T1-S02 -->
3. Replace buffer with 70% (v/v) ethanol in nuclease-free water for permeabilization. Fixed cells can be stored in this solution at 4°C for up to 2 weeks. For immediate use, permeabilize with 70% (v/v) ethanol in nuclease-free water for 1 hr at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T1-S03 -->

### LabelX Treatment

1. Rehydrate cells permeabilized with 70% (v/v) ethanol in nuclease-free water by washing twice with PBS for 5 min per wash at room temperature. Pre-incubate fixed cultured cells with 20 mM MOPS buffer for 5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T2-S01 -->
2. Prepare LabelX as described in Reagents and Solutions, then dilute in 20 mM MOPS buffer to the desired concentration. For nearly complete RNA retention, use a final Label-IT amine concentration of 0.006 mg/ml. For smFISH experiments, recommend using 0.006 mg/ml (a 1:150 dilution from the LabelX stock solution). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T2-S02 -->
3. Remove the preincubation MOPS buffer and add LabelX in MOPS buffer to the fixed cultured cells. Use 80 μl for cells grown in removable-chamber cover glass and 120 μl for cells grown in Nunc Lab-Tek chambered cover glasses. Incubate overnight at 37°C. Afterwards, wash twice with PBS at room temperature for 5 min each. At this stage, cells can be temporarily stored at 4°C in PBS for up to a week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B14-T2-S03 -->

## Gelation (ExFISH Cultured Cells)

### Chamber Prep

1. For Grace removable-chamber cover glass: Use the chamber cover glass removal tool to remove the top wells, leaving the black silicone gasket. Leave 40 μl of PBS inside the well to keep cells hydrated. For Lab-Tek chambered cover glass: Glue the bottom of the cover glass to a 1-mm-thick microscope glass slide using epoxy glue for mechanical support. After curing, use a razor blade to pry apart the cover glass from the top wells, leaving the plastic gasket. Leave 100 μl PBS inside the well to keep cells hydrated. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T0-S01 -->

### Gelling Solution Prep

1. Prepare gelling solution for ExFISH by diluting VA-044 to a final concentration of 0.5% (w/v) in monomer solution (dilute stock 1:50). For example, to prepare 1 ml, add 20 μl VA-044 solution and 40 μl water to 940 μl monomer solution. Prepare at 4°C and use immediately. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T1-S01 -->
2. In a cold block or on ice, distribute the gelling solution for ExFISH into 200-μl aliquots in microcentrifuge tubes. Degas for 10 min in a vacuum desiccator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T1-S02 -->

### Gelation

1. Remove any remaining PBS from the wells on the cover glasses and add the degassed gelling solution for ExFISH. Use 40 μl for Grace removable-chamber cover glass and 200 μl for Lab-Tek chambered cover glass. Place the cover glass in a vacuum desiccator and degas for another 10 min. Meanwhile, prepare a glass slide covered in Paraﬁlm as the lid; ensure the Paraﬁlm surface is flat, clean, and free of folds to prevent the gel from sticking. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T2-S01 -->
2. To humidify the chamber, add a small amount of water to the bottom of a Tupperware container. Position an empty 24-well plastic bottom plate at the very bottom to provide a raised platform. Place the cover glass with cells and gelling solution on this platform. Ensure the water level is much lower than the height of the 24-well plate so the sample remains well above the water. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T2-S02 -->
3. Perform nitrogen perfusion of the sample inside the Tupperware. Remove tape seals, insert a nitrogen line through one inlet, and leave the other open to allow air to escape. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T2-S03 -->
4. Following nitrogen perfusion, seal the two inlets with tape. Place the Tupperware containing the sample in a 60°C incubator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B15-T2-S04 -->

## Sample Expansion for Imaging

### Imaging Prep

1. Place the gel-embedded, digested sample in PBS (e.g., end of step 30 in Basic Protocol 1, end of step 25 in Basic Protocol 2, step 17 in Basic Protocol 4, or step 13 in Basic Protocol 5) in a petri dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B16-T0-S01 -->
2. Use a dissection microscope or a wide-field microscope with a low-magnification objective (e.g., 4× or 10×) to find the region of interest. For ExFISH samples, this should be done before staining with FISH probes (i.e., before step 18 in Basic Protocol 4 or step 14 in Basic Protocol 5). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B16-T0-S02 -->
3. Under the microscope, use a razor blade to remove excess gel (e.g., away from the region of interest). Cultured cell ExFISH samples may also need to be trimmed axially to reduce thickness (see steps 18 to 21 in Basic Protocol 4). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B16-T0-S03 -->
